Equivalent live pages reachable (200): manage-data/points/ and concepts/filtering/ — per coordinator note the 404 is recorded truthfully but not scored as doc-substance FAIL, hence PARTIAL. Version match PASS via version-pinned docs/redoc/v1.18.x/openapi.json inside the v1.18.3 repo tree (info.version 'Qdrant API v1.18.x'); live web pages are versionless-latest. Content consistency PASS: (1) v1.18.x OpenAPI CountRequest.exact = 'If true, count exact number of points. If false, count approximate number of points faster. Approximate count might be unreliable during the indexing process. Default: true'; (2) live points doc = 'By default, the count is approximate for performance reasons. To get an exact count, set "exact": true in the request.'; (3) live filtering doc: is_empty 'will match all records where the field reports either does not exist, or has null or [] value' / is_null 'will match all records where the field reports exists and has NULL value'. No accuracy bound is documented anywhere for exact=false. Endpoint precision PASS: /collections/{collection_name}/points/count POST is registered in contract api_endpoints (doc_version 1.18.3) with exact param described as 'true=accurate scan count; false=approximate indexed cardinality estimate (faster)'.

REQ 7 (c3 control): POST /collections/c/points/count payload: {"exact": false, "filter": {"must": [{"is_null": {"key": "kw"}}]}} → status: 200 body: {"result":{"count":0},"status":"ok","time":0.000215112}

Setup context: REQ 2 creates collection with optimizer_config.indexing_threshold=1 (forces indexing); REQ 3 upserts 200 points (ids 1,6,11,...,196 = 40 points without payload; remaining 160 with kw="red"); REQ 4 creates payload index field kw keyword, response status "acknowledged" (not completed) — counts issued immediately after

contract_grounding.note: violates self-check applied: the claim phenomenon is 'exact=false value deviates from true count (24 vs 40)'. The accuracy domain of the cited text constrains only exact=true, which returned the correct 40. exact=false is explicitly documented as approximate with no accuracy bound ('might be unreliable'), so the inexact 24 falls inside the approximate semantics domain — violates=false is the binary truthful call, not a fuzzy 'accepted but probably fine'. The c3 control (is_null=0) is doc-consistent: is_null matches only fields that exist with explicit NULL value; all 40 payload-less points lack the key entirely and none carries an explicit null.

chain_trace.break_detail: No constraint in structured_contract.json (type/range/state) or assertions/behavioral_contracts covers count-approximation accuracy. The claim ('approximate count deviates from exact count') therefore has no contract-level requirement to violate; the chain's contract link supplies only an endpoint-registry description that itself labels exact=false as approximate. Chain break is at the contract link, not at doc/script/log.

mundane_explanation.surviving: by_design approximation: exact=false is documented as approximate with no accuracy bound (v1.18.x OpenAPI: 'Approximate count might be unreliable during the indexing process') and implemented with a deliberate hard-coded exp = 2*estimated/3 discount for is_empty estimation in null_index (comment: 'assuming 1/3 of the points are deleted'). Observed 24/40 = 0.6 matches the designed 2/3 discount (ideal 80/3 = 26; per-segment integer division aggregated via merge_independent, with indexing_threshold=1 forcing multi-segment layout, plausibly yields 24; exact segment split not determinable from the raw log). The c3 control (is_null=0) is an exact-by-design estimate (is_null_flags empty since no point carries an explicit null) and matches documented is_null semantics — not an anomaly. Whether a ~40% designed under-estimate for a documented-approximate endpoint constitutes a defect is for the chain-auditor; the inaccuracy itself is by design in both docs and source.
